fullPassage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor 'time is a beggar,' the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor 'time is a beggar,' the audience is <u>unlikely</u> to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 unlikely와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 정답 ① probable(~할 것 같은). unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은)의 반의어이다.
det.analysis:
unlikely는 '~할 것 같지 않은, 가능성이 낮은'이라는 뜻이에요.

✅ ① probable(~할 것 같은) ←정답. unlikely의 반대말이에요.
❌ ② impossible(불가능한): '가능성이 낮은'과 달리 '완전히 불가능'이라 정도가 지나쳐요.
❌ ③ uncertain(불확실한): 반대말이 아니에요.
❌ ④ rare(드문): 빈도의 뜻이라 달라요.
det.tip: unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은) ↔ probable/likely(~할 것 같은)

questions.passage:
(A) Shakespeare is beloved in part because the meaning of his <u>works</u> is not immediately obvious. Readers often return to them again and again.

(B) Technological creators want to show clearly how the metaphor <u>works</u> at first glance. Users should not have to wonder about it.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 works가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) his works = 작품(창작물), (B) how the metaphor works = 작동하다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 작품 — (B) 작동하다 ←정답. (A)는 셰익스피어의 '작품'이라는 명사, (B)는 은유가 어떻게 '작동하는지'라는 동사예요.
❌ ① (A) 작동하다: his 뒤라 명사 '작품'이 맞아요.
❌ ② (A) 직장: 문맥과 맞지 않아요.
❌ ④ (B) 노력하다: how ~ works는 '작동하다'예요.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "ordinary written or spoken language that does not have the formal structure of poetry"

det.korean: 정답 ④ prose(산문). 시의 형식적 구조가 없는 일반적인 글/말을 뜻한다.
det.analysis:
정의는 '시의 형식적 구조가 없는 일반적인 글이나 말'이에요.

✅ ④ prose(산문) ←정답. 시가 아닌 보통의 글을 뜻해요. 본문의 'Shakespeare's prose'에서 쓰였어요.
❌ ① poetry(시): 형식적 구조가 있는 글이라 반대예요.
❌ ② rhyme(운율): 시의 요소예요.
❌ ③ drama(희곡): 연극 대본이라 달라요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 정답 essentially(본질적으로). 형용사 essential이 뒤의 related(관련된)를 꾸미므로 부사 essentially로 바꾼다.
det.analysis:
빈칸은 형용사/과거분사 related(관련된)를 꾸미는 자리예요. 이런 자리에는 부사가 와요.

essential(본질적인)은 형용사이므로, 부사 essentially(본질적으로)로 바꿔야 related를 꾸밀 수 있어요.

따라서 정답은 essentially예요.
det.tip: 형용사(essential) → 부사(essentially): 뒤의 형용사/분사를 꾸밀 때

questions.passage: Technological metaphors are realized in digital artifacts that are __________ (active) doing things. They forcefully change a user's meaning horizon.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 정답 actively(능동적으로). 동사 doing을 꾸미므로 형용사 active를 부사 actively로 바꾼다.
det.analysis:
빈칸은 뒤의 동사 doing(하고 있는)을 꾸미는 자리예요. 동사를 꾸미는 것은 부사예요.

active(능동적인)는 형용사이므로, 부사 actively(능동적으로)로 바꿔야 doing을 꾸밀 수 있어요.

따라서 정답은 actively예요.
